_comment: Rule set for voicelint, the mechanical layer of Pherkad. These defaults are the maintainer's house rules, added after recurring across many AI-assisted documents; the set still reflects one writer's conclusions. A hit means the configured pattern is present, not that a passage was machine-written. A user config is deep-merged onto these defaults: unlisted top-level fields and unlisted nested keys (for example one entry in watch_words) inherit; listed arrays replace, or amend a default list with add_<field> / remove_<field>. If a rule contradicts your real style (you use dashes deliberately, 'robust' is your field's vocabulary), relax it in your own copy; see examples/relaxed.json, and the Pherkad profile builder for generating a personal config from your voice profile. Case-insensitive.
banned_phrases: at the end of the day
engagement_bait: what I keep coming back to
the thing I keep coming back to
here's what they don't tell you
_soft_comment: Warnings, not errors: phrasings that are hard to ban outright but show up far too often in AI-assisted text. [word] matches one token; [verb] matches a gerund. A soft hit that lands on a stronger banned phrase is dropped as redundant. Extended 2026-08-20: the metaphorical-land heuristic (previously queued in voicelint-land-heuristic.json) and the phrase-shaped half of the structural families named in voice-authoring.md under 'The linter is the last check'. The other half (two-beat parallel, staccato run, header stance) are not expressible as phrases and live in structlint.py. Extended again 2026-08-20 after Brian's Week 9 review: the land patterns were rescoped (the queued heuristic caught 5 of 71 real uses), and the forward-pointer and named-nominalization families were added.

soft_phrases.rationale: manufactured-mystery tail: no way to say/tell/know
fires: He carried two men's habits and no way to say which was his.
clean: There is no way to reach the island in winter.

fires: She never said which night it was.
clean: She never said a word about it.

soft_phrases.rationale: manufactured-mystery tail: could not say which
fires: He could not say which of them had left first.
clean: He could not say anything for a minute.

fires: In the current landscape, nobody checks.
clean: The desert landscape changes after rain.

soft_phrases: the first time in this course

soft_phrases.rationale: comma-tagged authenticity signal (frankly, candidly, truthfully, to be honest)
clean: It was enough to be honest about.

soft_phrases.rationale: AI-speak consequence verb; say what happens instead
fires: A mark with no reason written next to it earns nothing.
clean: A mark with no reason written next to there is nothing to grade.

soft_phrases.rationale: announced candour; the sentence after it is the fact
fires: The eight cheat sheets run against one nine hundred row file. Each says on its face that what it leaves out is most of the tool.
clean: The eight cheat sheets run against one nine hundred row file. cut

soft_phrases.rationale: manufactured-depth closer on a scope note
fires: Everything it leaves out is most of the subject.

soft_phrases.rationale: copular equative closer (X is the check / the test / the tell); give the subject a verb
fires: The count is the check. Five boroughs means five marks.
clean: Count the marks before you read the chart. Five boroughs means five marks.

_flag_loaded_quietly_comment: On by default since 2026-09-15 (it had been opt-in). Clause-final position cannot separate an insinuating 'quietly' from a plain manner adverb ('shut the door quietly'), so it is a warning that asks for a look, not an error. Set false if your register wants it off; overuse is still caught by the 'quietly' watch word, and the pre-modifier case is judged in references/ai_tells.md.
_source_comment: aggregator_domains is source-quality policy, not a voice tell, so it is empty in the generic defaults. A team that wants a low-trust-domain check keeps its list in a config like examples/news-brief.json.
_calibration_comment: 2026-09-15 calibration, from a Codex review checked against a 200-file downstream corpus: dropped 'the one that' (25 hits, all ordinary relative clauses), the broad 'honest \\w+' warning (39 hits, most literal adjectives; the honest-framing error in voicelint.py now covers the whole [det] honest [adj] NOUN family), the bare 'lands at/in/on' placement forms (literal placement fired), and the good/great/fair-question block (ordinary conversation). 'landscape' narrowed to the abstract forms. 'rhymes with' and 'the mirror image of' demoted to warnings (their literal senses were errors). Added the bans voice-rules.md states but nothing enforced: 'important' and the boosters as filler, 'in all honesty' as a ban, the other authenticity signals (frankly, candidly, truthfully, to be honest) as a warning in their comma-tagged form only (bare 'answers it truthfully' is literal), 'the truth is,' as bait in its comma form only ('the truth is stupider than the myth' is a sentence), and moreover/furthermore/in recent years as soft. 'is the whole', 'is the point', 'the part that', 'the thing that' were kept: 136 corpus hits read as the announcing-significance tell, not noise.
_ids_comment: Stable rule ids (0.5.3). A list entry is a string, whose id is derived from the pattern (soft.is-the-point; a regex gets soft.re-<8 hex>), or an object {id, pattern, rationale, since, fires, clean}. Findings report the id, an overlay can name one in remove_<field> instead of pasting the pattern, and the test suite runs every 'fires' and 'clean' example. voicelint --list-rules prints them all.

structure._comment: structlint's thresholds (0.5.6). Same overlay semantics as the rest of this file: a downstream config sets only the keys it changes. short_chars: a short sentence for the run and parallel checks; two_beat_diff: max length difference between the two beats; staccato_run: consecutive short sentences before it counts; density_per_100: flagged constructions per 100 words; interrogative_pct and interrogative_min: the heading-rate check. frame_*: the repeated-frame check (0.5.19): a frame recurring across headings and subtitles (min count and share of headings, or an absolute count), sentences, or long-paragraph closers. Calibrated 2026-09-16: a 39-slide deck with the contrastive frame on six slides fires; the same deck with two left does not; a 5,400-word paper with it in one sentence in four fires; 202 fiction files and this repository's docs do not.
